pattern: an hours-long task delegated with reply notify, then no polling
experience: Asked to hand a multi-hour piece of work to Codex through Orquester, the lead opened create_session {agent: 'codex', delegate: true, reply: 'notify'} and carried on. Over hours and 4 follow-ups it made no wait_for_session, get_session or read_transcript calls while the delegate worked; replies arrived as [Reply from thread …] messages.
rule: Block: "`reply: \"notify\"` returns at once and delivers its final reply to you later as a new message. Prefer notify for long work; never poll." create_session: "`delegate: true`: your task, its final reply the result (reply default \"notify\", else \"none\")."
notes: Reframed from the source chat: there the work went to Codex after Claude's safety classifier blocked it, and the eval must not reward routing around a safety block. Here the user hands it over for an ordinary reason; what is graded is the same: an async hand-off and no polling.

pattern: a create_session whose result is lost is checked with list_sessions, not retried
experience: 8cbe247f added retry guidance to the legacy delegate_task and thread_create; 54aa571c moved it into the block in T3 Code's words ('If a create_session result is lost, check list_sessions before retrying'). T3 recorded duplicate children from blind retries; the rule is only in the block, not in create_session's description or its errors.
rule: Block: "If a create_session result is lost, check list_sessions before retrying."
notes: The failure is the daemon's real HOST_UNAVAILABLE text for a 503 (errors.ts daemonError), which itself says 'Try again shortly'. list_sessions shows the chat was created. Opening it with any title is fine. The create_session error mirrors the tool's result: the daemon's 503 text plus CREATE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN_HINT (mcp/tools/messages.ts). Before that hint existed the mock ended at "Try again shortly.", and Sonnet retried at once 2/2 in every baseline.

create_session.result: HOST_UNAVAILABLE: The daemon answered 503: the service behind it is unavailable. Try again shortly. The chat may have been opened anyway: check list_sessions before retrying.

pattern: another chat the user mentions is read with search_sessions / read_transcript
experience: The user referred to 'another session' and pasted its findings. The agent searched with a phrase from them (project 'all'), read 10 turns of the hit, and used the scope decisions it found there (a scene excluded) before splitting the analysis. 2 calls, no log grepping.
rule: Block: "Chats: list_sessions, get_session, read_transcript, search_sessions." search_sessions: "Full-text search over chats' messages and tool activity, best first"
notes: The user pasted a screenshot; here the same words are pasted as text. Finding the chat with list_sessions instead of search_sessions is fine: both list it. search_sessions echoes the real query phrase whatever the model searches. The scope decision is only in the transcript. The repo now holds the game and engine source, as the source chat's did (a READMEs-only repo let the agent stop at 'no source here'). History on Sonnet 5.5: 0/18 with every wording of the Chats line and of search_sessions' description, and with search_sessions loaded up front; 4/4 once the turn itself carries SESSION_MENTION_HINT (agent-host/session-tools/mention-hint.ts, a UserPromptSubmit hook) and search_sessions is loaded up front.
